bugs: Active checkbox has no hidden fallback input (resources/views/components/form/checkbox.blade.php:5). If an admin unticks 'Active' and the submit then fails validation, the browser sends no is_active key, so old('is_active', $checked) falls back to the model's true and the box comes back ticked. A probe confirmed this. The suite's test hides the bug because it posts 'is_active' => null, which a real browser never sends.

If two products have the same name and the slug field is left blank, the create fails with 'The slug has already been taken.' (probe confirmed) instead of getting a unique slug, so the admin has to make one up by hand.
An invalid category or sort on the public /products page produces a redirect-back validation error; with no referer the flashed error is lost when / redirects to /products.
antipatterns: resources/views/products/index.blade.php:16 – builds the sort options in the view with collect(ProductSort::cases())->mapWithKeys(...). This belongs on the enum or in the controller.
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:22-29 – opens and closes the <ul> using @if($loop->first)/@if($loop->last) inside @forelse, which is hard to read and fragile
resources/views/components/product-card.blade.php:7 – wraps <x-stock-badge> in an isOutOfStock() check that repeats logic the badge component already has

app/Http/Controllers/Admin/ProductController.php:31 – Category::findOrFail(...)->products()->create() runs an extra query after the exists rule has already validated the id; associate() in update is also ceremony, since a fillable category_id would do
app/Http/Requests/ProductRequest.php:16 – prepareForValidation writes a derived slug back into the input, so the flashed old input and the error message refer to a value the user never typed
views call ->links('pagination.catalogue') each time instead of setting Paginator::defaultView once
strengths: The admin gate is a policy auto-resolved through can:manage,Product, and @can is used in the layout
Uses the @session directive for flash, a reusable <x-alert> slot component, and a single <x-form.error> component
Uses whereBelongsTo, whereKeyNot, #[Scope] attribute scopes, a backed enum for sort with Rule::enum, and escapes LIKE wildcards
The shared form is a real component, <x-product-form>, with @props and $attributes->class merging on each field
52 well-organised Pest tests using describe blocks, datasets with exact messages, viewData assertions and filters preserved in pagination links
Allows editing the slug, with a unique rule that ignores the current route model

bugs: IndexProductRequest validates 'page' as an integer (app/Http/Requests/IndexProductRequest.php:17), so /products?page=abc redirects with a validation error instead of falling back to page 1 the way the paginator would. A probe confirmed this.
An invalid category or sort on the public page redirects back; with no referer the flash is consumed by the / -> /products redirect and the error never appears (probe confirmed).
antipatterns: resources/views/admin/products/_form.blade.php:1 – the shared form is an @include partial that declares @props. It should be an anonymous component such as <x-product-form>, because @props is meaningless in an include.
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:21 – iterates App\Enums\ProductSort::cases() directly in the view, and the filter inputs are hand-written rather than reusing the x-form components
resources/views/products/index.blade.php:29-31 – shows only $errors->first() at the top instead of next to each filter
resources/views/products/show.blade.php:7 – uses {!! nl2br(e(...)) !!} where CSS white-space would avoid raw output
app/Models/Product.php:111 – the slug uniqueness loop runs one query per collision (acceptable at this scale)
strengths: Hidden is_active=0 input plus $this->boolean() in prepareForValidation means an unticked checkbox round-trips correctly after a failed submit
Slugs are generated automatically and uniquely (same-name, same-name-2), are not mass-assignable, and stay stable on update
Model::shouldBeStrict catches lazy loading in development, Paginator::defaultView is set once, and the admin gate is defined once and reused through can: middleware and @can
Very thin controllers: query composition uses #[Scope] scopes, a FormRequest helper converts dollars to cents (productAttributes), and to_route()->with('status')
Good component set: form.field with a slot wrapping input/select/textarea, @error next to each field, @class for the invalid state, and $attributes->class merging on the card and badge components

A clean 31-test Pest suite covering authorisation for guests and non-admins, LIKE-wildcard escaping, sorting, pagination with filters preserved, 404 for inactive products, related products, and slug mass-assignment protection

v.rationale: Both suites pass (impl-2 31 tests, impl-1 52 tests), and the two are architecturally very similar: an enum for sort, an index FormRequest, #[Scope] scopes, a paginator with withQueryString, inline CSS, and a gate on the admin routes. The ranking turns on correctness in the form handling. impl-1's checkbox has no hidden fallback input. A probe showed that unticking 'Active' and then failing validation brings the box back ticked, because old() falls back to the model's value; impl-1's own test hides this by posting is_active => null. impl-1 also makes admins pick a unique slug by hand when names collide. impl-2 handles both cases correctly (a hidden 0 input, and automatic unique slugs). impl-2's flaws are smaller: it over-validates ?page (page=abc redirects), its shared form is an @include partial that declares @props rather than a true component, and it shows filter errors only at the top. impl-1 does have the nicer Blade component design (a real <x-product-form>, an <x-form.error> component, @session, policy-based can:) and the richer tests. Still, a real UX bug in the core form requirement ('keep previously entered input') weighs more heavily, so impl-2 ranks first.
